## ✨ Highlights

- 🛡️ **An update is checked block by block as it's written** ([#492](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/492), [#506](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/506)). A node checked an update's kernel image - its signature, which pins the root filesystem's dm-verity root hash - but wrote `rootfs.squashfs` and `rootfs.verity` without checking them against that hash. A damaged or swapped one was refused only at the next boot, from the slot the node had just switched to: no root, no janusd, no automatic revert (🔒 JANUS-2026-007). Now `rootfs.verity` is checked against the signed root hash first, then each block of `rootfs.squashfs` before it's written. A refused bundle leaves the node running, and says which file is wrong.
- 📦 **128 MiB slots for new disks** ([#506](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/506), [when a release doesn't fit](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/guide/updates.md#when-a-release-doesnt-fit)). The image with every extension had come within 0.4 MiB of the 64 MiB slots every disk was made with. Images, SD cards and `Install` now make 128 MiB slots. A disk keeps its slots for good: a node reads its own slots' size, and refuses a release that doesn't fit before anything is written, saying how to replace the node instead. Updates are streamed into the slot and never held in memory.
- ⚖️ **The image builder shows what an image takes of a slot** ([#507](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/507), [#505](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/505)): each extension's weight, and a meter of the image you pick against its slot. The Prometheus node exporter lost its debug information - half its weight - so the image with every extension is down from 63.6 to 57.8 MiB.

## ⚠️ Upgrade notes

- **Nodes installed before this release keep their 64 MiB slots.** Every image fits them today: the default one takes about 16 MiB, every extension together about 58 MiB. `janusctl version` shows a node's `Slot size`. To give a node 128 MiB slots, replace it: **Recycle** a cluster member the Controller made, or install a new node and move the old one's state to it ([replacing a node](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/guide/replacing-a-node.md)).
- **New images make bigger disks**: 1.2 GiB instead of 842 MiB. The qcow2 you download is the same size (the space is empty and stored sparsely). `Install` needs 384 MiB more disk.
- **An uploaded update now goes straight into the node's other slot.** This covers `janusctl lifecycle upload-release` and the Controller pushing a bundle to a node that can't download it. Until the update completes, that slot holds no release, and `lifecycle rollback` refuses it.
- **One operation on the slots at a time**: an update, a rollback or an upload while another one runs is refused - try again once it's done.
- **The update that brings this release is written by the release a node runs**, without the new check: take it over HTTPS (GitHub Releases, the image factory) or through the Controller.

## 🔒 Security

- **Janus itself** (nodes), its own code:
  - 🟡 medium [JANUS-2026-007](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/blob/v2026.11.03/security/fixes/JANUS-2026-007.json) - A root filesystem swapped or damaged in an update bundle left the node unable to boot, with no automatic revert. Anyone able to alter a bundle on its way - a node fetching an `http://` URL, a mirror, a server the bundle came from - could take down every node that updated from it. Running their own code was never possible: dm-verity refuses every block the signed root hash doesn't cover. Update every node, taking this update over HTTPS or through the Controller.

## ⚙️ Node

- **The update path** ([#506](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/506), [boot and A/B updates](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/internals/boot.md)):
  - `Upgrade` reads the kernel image's dm-verity table, refuses a root filesystem bigger than the slot, checks the hash tree against the root hash, then streams the root filesystem into the slot, each block checked first. A block refused within the first MiB leaves the slot as it was. Refused later, the slot holds neither release: `janusctl version` says so, and the node keeps running.
  - `Rollback` checks the other slot against the kernel image staged for it, and refuses one an update wrote part of. Before, such a slot left the node unable to boot.
  - `UploadReleaseFile` writes `rootfs.squashfs` straight into the inactive slot: STATE, 128 MiB on images, can be smaller than a slot. A new optional `size` field, which janusctl and the Controller send, refuses a file too big for the slot before anything is written.
  - `Install` checks the bundle against both kernel images before touching the disk, then streams it.
  - `VersionResponse.slot_bytes`, and `Slot size` in `janusctl version`.
- **The disk layout** ([the disk image](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/image/disk/README.md)): 128 MiB data slots; the hash partitions, the ESP and STATE are unchanged.

## 🏭 Image factory

- **Each part of an image is weighed when a release is built** ([#507](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/507)): the base, each HAProxy branch and each extension, squashed like the image, go into the release's catalog, along with the slots' size. The builder adds them up for the image you pick, shows each extension's weight, and says when an image is bigger than the 64 MiB slots of older disks.
- **The image with every extension must leave 8 MiB of a slot**: the release build fails otherwise.
